title: How Infinity Becomes Finite
description: A 6-step journey from pure consciousness through Māyā and the five coverings to the individual subject.

steps.narration: Consciousness is not a blank light — it is light that knows itself as light. This is the union of prakāśa and vimarśa, radiance and self-awareness. From this unitary pulsation, all reality unfolds.
steps.reflectionPrompt: Can you sense the difference between simply seeing an object and knowing that you see it? That self-knowing is vimarśa.

steps.narration: This pulsation is spanda — the eternal vibration of I-consciousness. Every thought, every perception, every moment of awareness is a pulse of spanda. It is not movement in time but the very dynamism of the absolute.
steps.reflectionPrompt: Observe your breath. Between the in-breath and the out-breath, is there a subtle pause — a presence that is not breathing but aware of breathing?

steps.narration: Through its own freedom, the one consciousness appears to divide. Māyā is the power of self-limitation by which the infinite becomes finite, the one appears as many. It is Śiva's play of concealment, like a single light refracted through a prism.
steps.reflectionPrompt: Notice the sense that you are 'inside' looking 'out' at a world separate from you. That boundary is not real — it is the effect of Māyā.

steps.narration: Māyā's five coverings further fragment awareness. Time contracts the eternal now into past and future. Destiny binds absolute freedom into cause and effect. Attachment turns fullness into the ache of wanting. Limited knowledge cuts omniscience into discursive thought. Limited agency confines omnipotence into small actions.
steps.reflectionPrompt: Pick one covering — time. The sense that 'time is passing' — who experiences time? Is the experiencer itself in time?

steps.narration: Take Rāga — the contraction of infinite fullness into the experience of lack. Before any particular desire, there is the baseline sense that something is missing. That unease is Rāga. It drives the endless reaching for objects that never finally satisfy, because the fullness you seek is what you already are.
steps.reflectionPrompt: The next time you feel desire arise — for anything — pause and look at the desiring itself before it fixes on an object. What does it feel like?

steps.narration: And Vidyā — the contraction of omniscience into limited knowing. Your knowledge is always partial, always through concepts, always within a framework. But the knowing in which all frameworks appear — that is not limited. Trace knowledge back to the knower, and the knower back to pure consciousness.
steps.reflectionPrompt: You know that you know. Who knows that? Keep going back.
